all_length_decoder_theorem.cone_invariant: The peeled matrix is a nonnegative integral unimodular path matrix.
consequences: all finite fixed-start path matrices are collision-free
central first-return matrices are pairwise distinct at every length
concatenated central return branches decode and segment uniquely
the central-return matrix monoid is free on its countable first-return generators
in this full-rank four-letter H(2) class, same-absolute-homology-matrix metaplectic cancellation cannot occur between distinct fixed-start branches
all_length_decoder_theorem.first_edge_invariant: For the true first edge, row_w(R)-row_l(R)=row_w(R_rest), componentwise nonnegative and nonzero.
all_length_decoder_theorem.name: FIXED_START_ALL_LENGTH_RAUZY_MATRIX_INJECTIVITY
all_length_decoder_theorem.peel_operation: Replace row_w by row_w-row_l, equivalently R <- R_e^(-1) R, then advance the labeled permutation.

projection_scope.current_absolute_homology_application: at every state of this H(2) class det(Omega)=1, hence Omega has full rank and relative homology equals absolute homology; a fixed symplectic basis change loses no matrix information
projection_scope.full_matrix_theorem: injectivity is first proved for the full four-by-four labeled Rauzy matrix B
projection_scope.general_warning: for a Rauzy class with a nontrivial relative-homology kernel, injectivity after projection to absolute homology does not follow from this decoder

all_length_decoder_theorem.proof_method: Induction on the entry sum; the algorithm is a two-sided inverse on the image of the fixed-start path-matrix map.
all_length_decoder_theorem.scope: fixed labeled start state and the full labeled Rauzy matrix are required; neither the state nor chronology may be discarded
all_length_decoder_theorem.statement: For a fixed labeled starting permutation, every finite directed Rauzy path is uniquely determined by its chronological matrix B.
all_length_decoder_theorem.termination_measure: The sum of all entries drops by the strictly positive loser-row sum at every peel and ends at sum(I)=4.
all_length_decoder_theorem.uniqueness_argument: The two candidates reverse the same rightmost label pair. If both winner rows dominated, the two rows would be equal; an image matrix is unimodular, so this is impossible.
